questions.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$

| $v=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(2)(1)-(1)(-2)}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$

| $v=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |

|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(2)(7)-(3)(5)}[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

$$

The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
questions.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-6-(-4)}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Vertices of a Polygon Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(0,2),(-3,3),(12,4),$ and $(7,3).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(-2,2)$
- $(1,-1)$
- $(4,4)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${P}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $P$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-0}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 12 & 7 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -6 & 8 & 4 \\ 4 & 6 & 8 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $P$ are $(-1,2),(-3,3),(4,4),(2,3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(-2,2),(-5,4),(-3,2),$ and $(0,0).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(-2,1)$
- $(0,0)$
- $(2,0)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${P}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $P$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3-2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $P$ are $(0,2),(-1,2),(-1,0),(0,0).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}7 & 10 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(10,5),(0,-5),$ and $(15,20).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(9,5)$
- $(0,1)$
- $(10,-7)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 20\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 20\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{35-30}[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}0 & 50 & -125 \\ 5 & -35 & 95\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 10 & -25 \\ 1 & -7 & 19\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(0,1),(10,-7),(-25,19).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(-21,0),(21,0),$ and $(0,3).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(0,-3)$
- $(3,1)$
- $(-3,3)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-7-0}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -21\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(-3,0),(3,0),(0,-3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(3,2),(14,6),$ and $(9,2).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(3,2)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(5,1)$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}3 & 14 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 14 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 14 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 14 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-0}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 14 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 14 & 9 \\ 2 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 10 \\ 2 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(-1,1),(2,3),(5,1).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

$$

$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by $T^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4-(-3)}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
